title: Being a good friend
hook: a friendship quiz, and the seven marks of a friend (AN 7.36)
tomorrow: why did the Buddha once walk off alone into an elephant's forest?

segments.voice: Yesterday, friends: the north, the good-hearted people you steer by. Today the list turns around and points at you.

Online friendship quizzes ask the easy things: their favorite color, their go-to order, their middle name. The Buddha's quiz is harder. In a short teaching in the Anguttara Nikaya, he names seven marks of a friend worth keeping. A friend gives what's hard to give. Does what's hard to do. Bears what's hard to bear. Tells you their secrets. Keeps yours. Doesn't leave you in trouble. And doesn't look down on you when you're down. Read it as a mirror, not a scorecard. Which one is hardest for you?
screen: `FAVORITE COLOR? GO-TO ORDER?` → `SEVEN MARKS OF A FRIEND.` → `A MIRROR, NOT A SCORECARD.`

segments.voice: Notice where the weight falls. Three of the seven start with hard: hard to give, hard to do, hard to bear. Friendship, here, is measured in the moments it costs something. Two marks are about trust running both ways: telling your secrets, and keeping theirs. A friend lets you see them, and guards what you have shown. And the last two are about the bad stretch: not leaving, and not looking down. That's the friend in need. Now this week, all of it, one line at a time. When love ends, the bond can stop, and the wish for their good can stay: kind at the end. Parents care by steering: guide them. Rahula's mirror, before, during and after: reflect first. Ryokan in the field all night: play. Kisa Gotami at every door: held gently. Four good-hearted friends, and a direction to steer by: north. Put them side by side and they make one picture of a person: someone who wishes well even at a distance, steers gently, looks before acting, plays with their whole heart, stays near grief, and shows up when it's hard. That's a good friend too. None of it needs a grand gesture. It fits inside an ordinary Tuesday.
screen: `HARD TO GIVE, DO, BEAR.` · `NOT LEAVING, NOT LOOKING DOWN.` · `SIX LINES FROM THIS WEEK.` · `ONE PICTURE OF A FRIEND.` · then, large: `THE FRIEND IN NEED.`

segments.voice: Go back over the seven marks slowly, one breath for each. When one catches, the one that feels hardest, stay there. Bring to mind a friend who needs exactly that from you right now, and picture one small, real way to give it. If no one comes to mind, rest on someone who has been that friend for you.
Being a good friend: the seven marks turned toward yourself, weighed in the moments that cost something.
Hold on to this: be the friend in need, on the hard day especially. Two of six, with a week behind you.

howItsDone: Buddhist teachers sometimes read the seven marks of a friend from the Anguttara Nikaya alongside the Sigalovada, as a way to look at the kind of friend one is.

match.prompt: seven marks, one week — tap the pairs.

fork.setup: a friend got cut from the team and is avoiding everyone. you're slammed this week. which mark of a friend fits best?
options: give them space; true friends wait to be asked before reaching out.
send a long text with advice on how to make the team next year.
show up for ten minutes: don't leave, and don't look down on them.
fork.reveal: the last two marks are exactly this: not leaving in trouble, and not looking down when someone's down.

trapdoor: what you thought: a good friend is someone fun to be around.
what it means: a good friend gives, does and bears what's hard, shares and keeps secrets, stays in trouble and never looks down.
what a scholar hears: AN 7.36, a short sutta of seven qualities, sits alongside DN 31's good-hearted friends as the canon's portrait of friendship.

being easy company and never asking for anything

chat.says: ava wants me to come with her to give jake his hoodie back. so awkward. do i have to go?
options: Go if you can. A friend does what's hard to do; you can just stand there with her.
Skip it. Good friends protect their own peace first; she can mail it.
Go, and tell Jake exactly what you think of him. That's real loyalty.
chat.meaning: The seven marks start with doing what's hard and not leaving a friend in trouble. Standing beside her is enough.

tie.story: The Buddha said a friend does what's hard to do and doesn't leave you in trouble.
tie.friend: Mai doesn't have to say a word to Jake; she just has to stand next to Ava.
tie.you: which of the seven marks is hardest for you right now?

Anguttara Nikaya.meaning: the numbered discourses, a collection of the Buddha's teachings

Rahula.meaning: the Buddha's son, who lived among the monks

Ryokan.meaning: a Zen monk and poet in Japan, known for playing with children

Kisa Gotami.meaning: a young mother whose grief the Buddha met with a mustard seed

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 7.36 (Mitta Sutta: a friend gives what is hard to give, does what is hard to do, endures what is hard to endure, reveals his secrets, keeps your secrets, does not abandon you in misfortune, does not despise you when you are down)

notes: AN 7.36 paraphrased; confirm the seven qualities and their order. 'Three of the seven start with hard' follows the Pali (duddadam dadati, dukkaram karoti, dukkhamam khamati); confirm.
